newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan army battles Moslem rebels.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan army battles Moslem rebels.

text.p: Uganda's army is still trying to repulse rebels it earlier said had been routed after they attacked the western town of Bundibugyo from the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo, a minister said on Monday.

Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi told Reuters that rebels of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) disguised as members of the Ugandan army had attacked the town with mortars on Sunday and the army was fighting to repulse them.
"The group which attacked Bundibugyo has broken into small groups after the attack," Mbabazi said.

"Our forces have chased them into the mountains after they lobbed three mortars into Bundibugyo. Our reinforcements were also attacked outside town again. There is no change in the situation, we will hunt them down."
Residents said the road between the western towns of Fort Portal and Bundibugyo remained closed on Monday after rebels laid mines.

The government-owned New Vision newspaper reported on Monday that up to 300 rebels took part in the attack on Bundibugyo and at least 20 soldiers had been wounded and taken to hospital after the attacks.
Officials say between 15,000 and 20,000 people have been displaced by the fighting and have fled into Bundibugyo town from surrounding areas.
"Togther with the ICRC we are trying to get from Fort Portal into Bundibugyo to do a registration," said Peter Oryema, director-general of the Ugandan Red Cross.
On Sunday, Mbabazi told reporters that the ADF, a rag-tag band of Moslem rebels, had been driven into the foothills of the Ruwenzori mountain range.
At least 40 civilians were killed by the ADF rebels when it first attacked last week.
Bundibugyo, a small town, is cut off from the rest of Uganda by a spur of mountains. The only road connecting it with the rest of Uganda has been under attack.
The Ugandan army commander, Major-General Mugisha Muntu, was directing operations in the Bundibugyo area, Kampala newspapers reported.

Mbabazi said about 700 ADF rebels had been killed since they launched their operations into western Uganda last November. He said the ADF was a small Moslem fundamentalist group which had been supported by the government of Sudan.
Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni met his army commanders in Western Uganda last week to discuss operations against the ADF.
